title: Does matching the opening text identify a seed?
question: Which seeds survive exact plaintext prefixes, and do they predict withheld text under included-seed, omitted-seed, wrong-generator and incorrect-crib controls?
summary: Two fixed hash generators and 4096 seeds each distinguish short-prefix agreement from complete plaintext recovery across 120 synthetic control cells.

scope.representation: All 95 known output rune indices from LP2-57, encrypted into six new synthetic additive ciphertexts.
scope.procedure: Search each generator dictionary for exact crib compatibility; retain all survivors and independently compare the full decoded passage and withheld suffix. Never select using withheld text.
scope.parameters: SHA-256/SHA-512; fixed ASCII domain and unsigned four-byte big-endian seed/counter; reject bytes >=232 then reduce mod 29; searched seeds 0..4095; planted seeds 17,4095,4096; cribs 2,4,8,16,32; correct or first-rune-plus-one crib; 120 cells.
scope.exclusions: No unsolved-page decoding, unknown-position search, language score, adaptive dictionary expansion, generator identification or population recovery probability.

finding: Matching two opening runes does not identify a seed: every control retains multiple candidates. Only the true generating pairs recover the complete withheld text. At four or more tested crib runes, included-pair searches retain only their true seed; other controls retain none.
limitations: One known passage and dependent deterministic fixtures; exact crib and alignment are supplied. Results apply only to two specified generators and dictionaries. Human review pending.
next_steps: Test separately declared offsets, uncertain cribs or alternative generator encodings with planted controls before applying them to unknown text.
